fields.h1: Build Media Consumption Survey Questions and Media Diaries
fields.hero_description: Build media consumption survey questions about news, podcasts, and video, with every answer saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Media Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the table behind it, and a follow-up prompt changes either one before the next wave goes out.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for each medium

Name your audience and the media you track, like local news and podcasts. Emergent drafts how-often and which-device questions for each, and you edit any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that skip what people never use

A respondent who says no to podcasts never sees the podcast block. Each person answers only about the media they used, so the results table has no blank rows to clean up.
fields.feature_3:
A 7-day diary with an evening reminder

Turn the survey into a daily media diary. Each participant gets an email reminder at 8 p.m. to log the minutes spent on each medium, and no reminder once that day's entry is in.
fields.feature_4:
Every entry in a database you own

Every response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the medium and the survey wave. Put this spring's podcast numbers beside last fall's without merging two exports.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

People answer one question per screen on a phone, at breakfast or on the train home. A yes or no on each source is one tap, and minutes get a number pad, not a text box.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code you can take

Run the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and paid for in credits. Responses have no cap, and paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Readers up before 8 a.m. get the email at 6:30

The Ashgrove Gazette sends its morning email at 11 a.m. Its reader survey asks which sources each reader used for local news in the past 7 days, and what time they first read it. Of the 612 readers who answer, 401 read local news before 8 a.m. The email now goes out at 6:30 a.m.
fields.tab_content_2:
Commuters get a 25-minute episode each week

Saltmarsh Audio publishes a 48-minute weekly history show. A survey in the show notes asks where people listen and how long a session lasts. Of 830 listeners who answer, 517 listen on a commute under 30 minutes. Next season, every episode runs 25 minutes.
fields.tab_content_3:
31 of 46 diaries ran under each phone's screen time

The 46 students in a Halvern College media studies class keep a 7-day media diary. Each day at 8 p.m., an email reminder asks for that day's phone minutes by type of app. On day 7, each student adds the week's total from the phone's screen time report. For 31 of the 46, the diary total is lower.
fields.tab_content_4:
Print loses its $2,400 budget to radio

Juniper Street Playhouse spends $2,400 a month on newspaper ads. After the spring run, it asks 1,800 ticket buyers where they heard about the show, with a yes or no for each channel. Of the 940 who answer, 388 heard it on local radio and 121 saw the newspaper ad. Next season, the full $2,400 goes to radio spots.

faq_plan.q: What are media consumption survey questions?
How do I create media consumption survey questions?

plan.angle: The searches behind media consumption survey questions want a usable question set for news, podcasts, video and social habits, and a way to trust the answers. Template lists stop at the questions. This page shows four real jobs (a newspaper readership survey, a podcast listener survey, a 7-day student media diary, and a theater's ad channel survey), each ending in a decision, and puts the craft advice where the lists fall short: a fixed recall window, one question per source, shuffled platform lists, and checking self-reports against logs.
tab_stories: The Ashgrove Gazette asks readers where they got local news in the past 7 days; 612 answer, 401 read it before 8 a.m., and the morning email moves from 11 a.m. to 6:30 a.m.
Saltmarsh Audio puts a listener survey in its show notes; 830 listeners answer, 517 listen on a commute under 30 minutes, and the weekly episode is cut from 48 to 25 minutes.
A Halvern College media studies class keeps a 7-day media diary; 46 students log their minutes each evening, and on day 7, 31 of 46 logged fewer minutes than their phone's screen time report showed.

Juniper Street Playhouse asks 1,800 ticket buyers how they heard about the last show; 940 answer, 388 name local radio against 121 for the newspaper ad, and the $2,400 monthly print budget moves to radio.
